newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shrs end broadly stable on some profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Lima shrs end broadly stable on some profit-taking.

text.p: Shares on the Lima stock exchange ended broadly stable Tuesday as players took profits in the mining sector following a bull run but bought other leading stocks, brokers said.
Miners were expected to dip again Wednesday, but continued gains in other blue chip shares were seen keeping the market stable overall, they added.

Tuesday, the General Index fell 0.13 percent to 2,060.9 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index edged up 0.02 percent to 2,986.2 points, according to preliminary figures given at the market's close.
In a total of 2,938 trades, volume was 53.3 million soles ($20.1 million), brokers said.
Investors finally decided to take profits in polymetallic miners Atacocha and Morococha that have led this month's explosive run in the mining sector, brokers said.
Atacocha fell 3.56 percent to 2.44 soles on volume of 716,000 shares, while Morococha dropped 5.10 percent to close at 6.70 soles on 141,000 shares.

"The stabilizing corrections are logical in the market," Marcial Aleman of local brokerage Abaco said. Considering the sector's gains this year -- above 170 percent -- Tuesday's falls "were very small," he added.
Benchmark Telefonica del Peru led other leading stocks up as it gained 1.56 percent to close at 6.49 soles on healthy volume of 1.4 million shares.
